world.h: Tanker hit off Qatar; casualties reported
world.b: A tanker was struck by multiple projectiles 58 miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, with casualties reported, UK Maritime Trade Operations said.
more: UKMTO reports a recent rise in attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
world.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles off north coast of Qatar, UKMTO says

world.h: Probe: accused Syrian general shielded in Lebanon
world.b: A BBC and NPR investigation found former Syrian general Bassam al-Hassan, wanted for crimes against humanity, lives in Lebanon protected and funded by U.S. and Lebanese authorities.
more: He oversaw Syria's chemical weapons program and advised Bashar al-Assad.
world.title: Syrian general accused of atrocities is protected by U.S. and Lebanon, NPR and BBC find

world.h: Israelis weigh reports Netanyahu was warned
world.b: As Israel marks three years since the Oct. 7 attacks, four people with direct knowledge told NPR that Netanyahu was personally warned about a potential Hamas attack.
more: Haaretz, The New York Times and The Atlantic first reported the warnings from regional allies.
Netanyahu has denied he was warned.
world.title: 3 years on, Israelis grapple with reports Netanyahu was warned before Oct. 7 attacks

world.h: Vance seeks 'meaningful' cut in Iran enrichment
world.b: Vice President JD Vance called for Iran to make a meaningful reduction in uranium enrichment capacity as part of a deal to end the war, Al Jazeera reports.
more: Experts say it may signal a softening of the earlier demand that Tehran abandon enrichment altogether.
Rubio reiterated Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon; Trump warned the war will end 'the nice way or the not-so-nice way'.

world.h: Bulgaria ends search for sunken ship's crew
world.b: Bulgarian authorities ended the search after finding no survivors from a cargo ship sunk by a drone strike off the coast on Tuesday.
more: Drones hit two commercial vessels as attacks on Black Sea shipping increase amid the Russia-Ukraine war.
Eighteen Turkish and Indian crew members were rescued from the second ship, which caught fire.

world.h: Three years since the Oct. 7 attack
world.b: Israelis gathered to mourn the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack that killed 1,200 people and saw 251 taken hostage.
more: The war it sparked has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza, including 21,000 children, Al Jazeera reports.
A ceasefire took effect Oct. 10, 2025, but attacks and killings have continued.

national.h: Isaias becomes first Atlantic hurricane of season
national.b: Isaias strengthened into a hurricane with 75 mph winds and is on track to make landfall between the Mississippi coast and the Florida Panhandle late Friday or early Saturday.
more: Forecasters warn of heavy rain and possible flash flooding.
national.title: Isaias strengthens into the first hurricane of the Atlantic season

national.h: Pediatricians renew call for raw milk ban
national.b: The American Academy of Pediatrics renewed its call for a nationwide ban on selling unpasteurized milk and raw dairy, citing serious risks for children, pregnant and immunocompromised people, ProPublica reports.
national.title: American Academy of Pediatrics Renews Call for Ban on Raw Milk

national.h: LA health officials target medical debt
national.b: Los Angeles County public health officials are treating medical debt like a disease to prevent, KFF Health News reports, as hospital bills crush patients.
national.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix

national.b: Eva Marie Saint, who won an Oscar for her first film, 'On the Waterfront,' and starred in Hitchcock's 'North by Northwest,' died at her Los Angeles home Tuesday.
more: Her acting work lasted well into her 90s.
national.title: Eva Marie Saint, star of 'On the Waterfront' and 'North by Northwest,' dies at 102

national.b: Tropical Storm Isaias could hit the Gulf Coast as a hurricane late Friday or early Saturday, hours before No. 2 Georgia plays at No. 6 Alabama with Trump planning to attend.
more: Forecasters say Isaias could become a hurricane by Thursday.
The SWAC moved Florida A&M's game at Alabama State to Friday morning.
national.title: Tropical storm threat churns planning for Georgia-Alabama game with Trump set to attend

national.h: Trump approves firing squad for Fort Hood shooter
national.b: Trump approved the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, NPR reports. It is set for Dec. 3 at Fort Hood.
more: It would be the first U.S. military execution in over six decades and the first by firing squad since World War II.
Hasan could delay it with a habeas corpus appeal.

national.h: Texas set to execute Jamaal Howard
national.b: Texas is set to execute Jamaal Howard, 46, for the 2000 killing of convenience store clerk Vickie Swartout, in what would be the nation's 30th execution this year.
more: It is the first scheduled U.S. execution since Tennessee's failed attempt to execute Christa Pike.
national.title: Texas set to execute Jamaal Howard for 2000 fatal shooting

national.h: Over 1,000 children buried at youth detention sites
national.b: NPR reports Georgetown University researchers are working to identify children who died at 40 reform schools and youth detention centers across the country.
more: Researchers have linked 16 families to children who died at a reform school in Cheltenham, Maryland.
The work is part of the Forgotten Children Initiative, underway since February.
national.title: Over 1,000 children are buried at juvenile detention centers nationwide

national.h: Flu season is starting unusually early
national.b: Flu activity began picking up in early September, NPR reports, earlier than the usual October or November start.
more: Positive flu tests in the West have risen steadily since about the start of September, says Johns Hopkins epidemiologist Caitlin Rivers.
Emergency department visits for flu have also been rising for weeks.
national.title: An early flu season means it might be time to think about a flu shot

national.h: Phoenix poet becomes hotline for homeless families
national.b: ProPublica reports 26-year-old advocate Austin Davis' AZ Hugs has become the unofficial emergency shelter hotline for homeless families in Maricopa County.
more: Most callers say they first tried 211, only to learn shelter could be months away.
Teachers, caseworkers, police and hospital workers have called asking for his help.
national.title: Homeless Shelters Around Phoenix Are Full. His Phone Is the Unofficial Hotline for Struggling Families.

politics.h: DNC sues Trump over taxpayer-funded ads
politics.b: The Democratic National Committee sued Trump over publicly funded TV ads it says promote his policies ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms.
politics.title: Democrats sue US President Trump over taxpayer-funded ad campaign

politics.h: Trump pitches 'Camp David' at his Florida golf club
politics.b: Trump proposed turning his West Palm Beach golf course into a presidential retreat for his successors, calling it 'sort of a Camp David.'
politics.title: Trump proposes Camp David-style presidential retreat at his private Florida golf club

politics.h: Trump's $90 Medicare rebate leaves millions out
politics.b: Trump says about 20.8 million Medicare enrollees will get one-time $90 payments toward Part B premiums, costing about $2 billion; critics call it a political stunt.
more: Fewer than a third of Medicare recipients qualify; about 35 million Medicare Advantage enrollees do not.
politics.title: Trump's $90 Medicare rebate rolls out, but millions aren't eligible. Critics see a political stunt

politics.h: Trump: 70 million kids get automatic 'Trump Accounts'
politics.b: Trump said 70 million children under 18 will have government-created 'Trump Accounts' to invest in stocks; parents must claim them on the program's website or app.
more: The 2025 tax law allows up to $5,000 a year in contributions, and seeds $1,000 for children born 2025 to 2028.
politics.title: WATCH: Trump announces eligible U.S. children automatically enrolled in Trump accounts

politics.h: Collins, Jackson clash in first Maine Senate debate
politics.b: Republican Sen. Susan Collins distanced herself from Trump, saying she is 'not exactly his favorite senator,' while Democrat Troy Jackson tied her to the president.
more: Jackson pointed to her vote to confirm Justice Brett Kavanaugh.
Democrats hope to flip the seat as they push for Senate control.
politics.title: What happened in the first Maine Senate debate between Collins and Jackson

international.b: Yemen's internationally recognised government says its 'Dawn of Yemen' counteroffensive has 'neutralised' 1,860 Houthi fighters, Al Jazeera reports.
international.title: Yemeni government forces claim 1,860 Houthis ‘neutralised’

international.h: South Korea vows action on fuel exports to Russia
international.b: South Korea's foreign ministry says it will take legal action if claims by a Zelenskyy adviser of illegal fuel shipments to Russia are confirmed.
international.title: South Korea pledges legal action over alleged fuel exports to Russia

international.h: Kosovo elects Justina Shiroka Pula president
international.b: Kosovo lawmakers elected Justina Shiroka Pula president in the first minutes of Wednesday, ending a standoff in parliament.
more: The ruling Vetevendosje Movement and the opposition PDK agreed on her candidacy ahead of a midnight deadline.
The vote came as protests against convictions of former KLA leaders filled the streets.

international.h: Palestinian killed in West Bank olive harvest attack
international.b: Palestinian health officials say a 44-year-old man was killed and 16 others wounded when settlers, protected by Israeli forces, attacked olive harvesters near Burqa, northwest of Nablus.
more: Several of the wounded were taken to hospitals in Tulkarem and Nablus, Wafa reported.

business.h: Stocks slide as Treasury yields hit 20-year high
business.b: Wall Street closed lower Wednesday as Treasury yields reached their highest in over 20 years and oil swung on renewed Iran war fears, Al Jazeera reports.
business.title: US stocks slide as oil prices fluctuate over renewed Iran war fears

business.h: Student loan autopay rate cut deadline extended
business.b: Borrowers now have until the end of 2026 to enroll in autopay and get a 1% interest rate reduction, which lasts through June 2028.
more: The original deadline was Sept. 30. Borrowers already on autopay get 0.75% more off.
business.title: Student loan borrowers have more time to reduce interest rates. Here's what to know

business.h: Trump loosens rules on farm 'dyed diesel'
business.b: An executive order makes dyed diesel, normally a farm fuel, more accessible through year's end to lower costs for heavy diesel users, NPR reports.
more: Diesel has been hit hard as fewer ships get through the Strait of Hormuz.

business.h: California weighs billionaire tax for health care
business.b: A California ballot measure would levy the nation's first wealth tax on billionaires to offset federal cuts to health care, food aid and education, Marketplace reports.
more: Critics call the temporary cash a giveaway to politicians, and it's unclear how much it would raise.

business.h: Mortgage rates hit near three-year high
business.b: Mortgage rates have reached their highest level in almost three years, NPR reports, making home buying harder while prices are already high.
more: Borrowing for a car has also become more expensive.
business.title: Here's the latest sticker shock: Borrowing for a mortgage -- or a car

science.h: Jurassic fossil shows early mammal chewing
science.b: A small middle Jurassic fossil from Inner Mongolia offers some of the oldest evidence of chewing, swallowing and suckling, distinctly mammalian traits, researchers say.
more: Paleontologists Zhe-Xi Luo and Thomas Martin studied the specimen at the Paleontological Museum of Liaoning.

science.h: Kagan and Soai win Nobel Prize in chemistry
science.b: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the chemistry Nobel for discovering non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.
more: The committee said they solved a century-old mystery: how homochirality can emerge spontaneously.
Their work has been decisive for chemists who design reactions to make pharmaceuticals.

sports.h: Dodgers beat Braves 4-1, advance to NLCS
sports.b: Andy Pages' two-run single in the seventh lifted the Dodgers past the Braves 4-1, winning the NL Division Series 3-1.
more: The Brewers are trying to close out their series against the Padres.
sports.title: 2026 MLB playoffs: Winners and losers as Dodgers, Rays, Brewers advance, Yankees eliminated in sweep

sports.h: Rays sweep Yankees, advance to ALCS
sports.b: Tampa Bay beat the Yankees 4-3 to win their AL Division Series 3-0 and eliminate New York.
sports.title: 2026 MLB playoff bracket: Schedule, scores, how to watch as Dodgers, Rays, Brewers advance, Yankees eliminated

sports.h: Guardians top White Sox 9-3 to stay alive
sports.b: Cleveland beat the White Sox 9-3 for Chicago's first loss of the playoffs; the White Sox lead the ALDS 2-1.
sports.title: 2026 MLB playoffs: Winners and losers as Dodgers, Rays, Brewers advance, Yankees eliminated in sweep

local.h: Mamdani joins Oct. 7 vigil amid Union Square protests
local.b: Mayor Zohran Mamdani attended a vigil marking the Oct. 7 attack as demonstrators waving Israeli and Palestinian flags filled Union Square under heavy police presence.
local.title: Mayor Mamdani attends Oct. 7 vigil amid protests in Union Square

local.h: Queens pharmacist charged in $31M Medicaid fraud
local.b: The owner of two Jackson Heights pharmacies was arrested on charges of a $31 million Medicaid drug-buyback scheme involving HIV prescriptions, the state attorney general said.
local.title: Queens pharmacy owner charged in alleged $31M Medicaid drugs fraud

local.h: NJ finds 1,100 more flawed voter registrations
local.b: Gov. Mikie Sherrill said her administration found about 1,100 more problematic voter registrations in its probe of the state's automatic voter registration system.
more: The probe into Motor Vehicle Commission registration errors began in July.
local.title: NJ probe finds about 1,100 more problematic voter registrations

local.h: MTA to put new fare gates at 150 stations
local.b: The MTA is moving ahead with a $1.1 billion rollout of modern sliding-door fare gates after testing them at 20 subway stations over the past year.
more: Officials say the gates have proven highly effective against fare evasion.
local.title: MTA moves ahead with $1.1B plan to put modern fare gates at 150 subway stations

local.h: Baby pushed from Bronx balcony now stable
local.b: An 8-month-old girl pushed from a 15th-floor Bronx balcony with her mother is in stable condition, and police have identified a man wanted in the case.
more: Her mother, 23-year-old Nathaly Ramirez, was killed Tuesday.
local.title: NYPD identifies man wanted in connection with deadly Bronx balcony push

local.h: Suspects in detective stabbing caught in Mass.
local.b: Two suspects in last week's stabbing of an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx were found hiding in a basement in Lynn, Massachusetts, police said.
more: D'Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24, were arrested by fugitive task force detectives.
local.title: Suspects in off-duty NYPD detective's stabbing found hiding in Massachusetts basement

local.h: Delaney Hall protest figure freed from ICE
local.b: Martin Soto, the Peruvian man at the center of summer protests at Newark's Delaney Hall, was released from ICE custody after a federal judge's order.
more: The judge cited his conditions and more than 200 days in detention.
local.title: NJ immigrant at the center of Delaney Hall protests released from ICE custody

local.h: Unlicensed Bronx doctor charged with murder
local.b: Luis Rojas Cabrera, 56, now faces a depraved indifference murder charge in the death of a 27-year-old patient during an anti-aging treatment, police say.
more: He was first arrested in July, days after Elizabeth Baron died.
local.title: NYPD says unlicensed doc has been charged with murder in 27-year-old patient death

local.h: ICE arrests near 40,000 across NY and NJ
local.b: ICE has made more than 19,500 arrests in New York state and nearly 18,000 in New Jersey during Trump's second term, Gothamist reports from new government data.
more: The arrests are largely of Latin American immigrant men without criminal histories.
local.title: Nearly 40K and counting: Here’s where ICE arrested immigrants across NY and NJ

local.h: Crashes pile up on Central Park's car-free loop
local.b: Three people have died in crashes on Central Park's 6-mile loop since June as more than 100,000 people use the park each day, Gothamist reports.
more: On Monday a 71-year-old cyclist fell near 84th Street while avoiding an off-leash dog.
local.title: Central Park's car-free loop is busier than ever. Crashes keep piling up.

local.h: NYC to spend $9M on youth gender-affirming care
local.b: New York City plans to spend nearly $9 million on local groups providing gender-affirming care to minors, part of a $15 million Mamdani administration pledge.
more: It follows deals by NYU Langone and Mount Sinai with the Trump administration to stop such care for minors.
local.title: NYC moves to spend nearly $9M of gender-affirming care fund for minors
